title: Dispatch: create, hold, schedule and close calls
summary: Follow a call from a complete initial entry through pending or scheduled dispatch, operational updates and historical closeout.
prerequisites: Call creation and editing rights; prepared priorities, types and department field policies.
Training contacts, protocols, destination POIs, templates and linked calls.
Configured geocoding for address, what3words or Plus Code demonstrations; prepared media and a valid test video stream.
Disposable historical data for archive insertion, deletion and any optional renumbering.

scenes.title: Create a complete call
scenes.capture_intent: Record the named screen and the described controls using staged training data; verify visible labels and permissions before performing the action.
scenes.narration: Open Calls and choose New Call. If the department has a useful call template, apply it first and review what it fills. Give the call a clear name, describe its nature, and choose the correct priority and type. Add the initial note and complete any department-required fields or custom form sections. The app waits for the department’s call settings before allowing a reliable submission. In the browser, the form offers keyboard shortcuts, including Control and Enter to create. Use the visible Create control while learning so you can review the complete entry before sending it.
scenes.practice: Prepare a training industrial alarm using its template, then verify the priority, type and required custom fields.

scenes.title: Locate the incident and its destination
scenes.capture_intent: Record the named screen and the described controls using staged training data; verify visible labels and permissions before performing the action.
scenes.narration: Use the location method that best describes the reported incident. Search an address and review the proposed match, enter both coordinates in decimal degrees, or use the map picker. Where the provider is configured, what3words and Plus Code offer additional search paths. Check the resulting pin against a known landmark; the presence of text alone is not confirmation of a usable location. Choose a Destination POI separately when the response has a known destination, such as a hospital or staging site. The destination does not replace the incident location. Provider availability and map permissions must be checked on the capture platform.
scenes.practice: Locate a remote SAR training point, then select a separate staging destination.

scenes.title: Connect the supporting information
scenes.capture_intent: Record the named screen and the described controls using staged training data; verify visible labels and permissions before performing the action.
scenes.narration: Add the caller or site contact, using contact search when the person or organization already exists. Review the contact information and any incident, reference or external identifiers your workflow uses. Select the relevant protocols and link an existing call when the events belong together. These links give the next operator more context than an isolated free-text note. Choose the intended recipients before creating the call; the allocation lesson explains the nearest-resource picker and run-card recommendations. Review the destination, recipients and supporting information together, because an accurate incident description still needs the right people and resources to receive it.
scenes.practice: Prepare a community welfare call linked to an earlier event and attach the appropriate department protocol.

scenes.title: Hold a call as pending
scenes.capture_intent: Record the named screen and the described controls using staged training data; verify visible labels and permissions before performing the action.
scenes.narration: When the situation needs review before notification, choose Save as pending on New Call. The call is saved and numbered, and the proposed recipients are retained, while notification and field-app visibility wait for dispatch. Open Pending Calls, search for the entry, and inspect its details before using Dispatch. Check the proposed recipients again if availability has changed. Cancel a pending entry only when your practice scenario calls for it. Pending is a deliberate holding state for a call taker or supervisor; it should not be mistaken for an active response simply because the call has a number.
scenes.practice: Hold a security alarm while a supervisor verifies it, then review the proposed dispatch.

scenes.title: Schedule, reschedule or dispatch now
scenes.capture_intent: Record the named screen and the described controls using staged training data; verify visible labels and permissions before performing the action.
scenes.narration: For a planned future response, set the scheduled dispatch date and time on the call form. The app requires the scheduled time to be at least fifteen minutes ahead. Open Scheduled Calls to search and inspect the planned response. Dispatch now brings the action forward when the situation changes. From call details, use Reschedule to choose an offered time preset or a custom date and time, then review the new schedule. Confirm the department’s time context during the exercise. Scheduled dispatch and a pending call serve different decisions, so choose the state that matches the actual operational plan.
scenes.practice: Schedule coverage for a public event, then move its start time and review the updated call.

scenes.title: Work through call details and protected information
scenes.capture_intent: Record the named screen and the described controls using staged training data; verify visible labels and permissions before performing the action.
scenes.narration: Open a call from Calls List and walk through its tabs. Info and Contact explain the incident, Protocols supplies attached guidance, and Dispatched shows the recorded allocation. Activity, History and Site Info add the event sequence, location history and site context. Use the protected-data reveal control when offered and complete the server’s required verification. Check-In shows the configured timer and accountability information; enable or disable timers only as your role permits. Set Active selects the call for the current working context. Edit changes the call, while Route opens the platform’s routing option for a usable location.
scenes.practice: Inspect a fire call’s site hazards, verify its dispatch rows and locate the check-in history.

scenes.title: Notes, images, files, audio and video
scenes.capture_intent: Record the named screen and the described controls using staged training data; verify visible labels and permissions before performing the action.
scenes.narration: Use Notes to add a meaningful operational update. Open Images to view evidence or add a training image from the gallery or camera with a note, then review the upload. Files can be opened or shared through the available platform tools, and Audio provides playback when a recording exists. On Video, add or edit an authorized test feed using its name, stream URL, camera type and format; inspect the remaining location and display options before saving. A saved feed entry does not prove its stream can play. Browser media support, camera access, native sharing and provider connectivity need their own checks.
scenes.practice: Attach a labeled exercise image and inspect a prepared drone feed without claiming live flight or transmission.

scenes.title: Close the response and preserve history
scenes.capture_intent: Record the named screen and the described controls using staged training data; verify visible labels and permissions before performing the action.
scenes.narration: Close Call asks for the outcome and closing note, with an option controlling notification. Review that choice before confirming. Search Archived Calls by year and the available status, type, priority and date filters to find the completed event. Add Archived Call records an incident that already happened: enter its logged and closed times, outcome, location, identifiers and historical recipients. It is saved as closed without dispatching those recipients. Optional recalculation changes the year’s numbering, so demonstrate it only in disposable data. Deletion is also a deliberate record-changing action; show its confirmation only when the exercise requires removal.
scenes.practice: Close an EMS training call, locate it in the archive and draft a separate historical event.

sector_examples.scenario: A medical call receives a hospital destination, check-in review and documented closeout.
A welfare visit is linked to earlier context and held for supervisor review.
Coordinates and a staging POI describe a remote response.
A pending alarm waits for verification before notification.
A planned standby is scheduled and adjusted as coverage changes.
An alarm template, custom fields and site contact support a plant response.
